title: Keyboard mapping stops working in WSLg windows.

status.label: Reproduce keyboard remapping failure in WSLg
status.detail: The original report described a one-time Caps Lock-to-Ctrl failure in WSLg; a later user reports persistent mapping failures in WSLg-hosted IntelliJ.

judgment.rationale: The original report on PowerToys 0.81.1 describes a one-time Caps Lock-to-Ctrl failure that recovered after restarting WSL. A later commenter describes persistent failures in WSLg windows, including IntelliJ running in WSL, while other applications work. These reports may represent different failures; the later comment does not provide current PowerToys, WSL, or WSLg versions or a precise mapping. Closed issue #5300 concerns WSL1 inside Windows Terminal and was redirected to a Windows Terminal issue, so it does not establish coverage for this WSLg report.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.81.1, WSL2 2.1.5.0, WSLg 1.0.60, and Windows build 22631.3737.
The original reporter says Caps Lock-to-Ctrl stopped working once in WSLg and began working again after restarting WSL.
A later commenter reports that remaps consistently fail in WSLg windows, including IntelliJ running in WSL, while normal applications still work.
The later commenter says restarting WSL, PowerToys, or the computer did not resolve the issue.
Closed issue #5300 concerns WSL1 inside Windows Terminal, a different environment and symptom.
judgment.recommended_action: Clarify the later user's current PowerToys/WSL versions and exact source-to-destination mapping, then reproduce in the affected WSLg application separately from ordinary Windows applications.

fix_assessment.rationale: If current Keyboard Manager remaps are dropped only by WSLg-hosted windows while continuing to work in Windows apps, investigate the host input-routing boundary and correct the confirmed WSLg-specific path.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Keyboard Manager remaps in WSLg windows
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager input events may not reach or be applied to WSLg-hosted application windows consistently; the reports do not identify whether the issue is in PowerToys or the WSLg input path.
plan: Reproduce a simple key-to-key remap in a WSLg application on current stable and compare with a Windows application.
Record the exact Windows, WSL, WSLg, target application, and remapping configuration for the persistent case.
Determine whether the mapping is lost at Keyboard Manager's hook, Windows focus/input routing, or the WSLg application boundary before choosing a code change.
Add regression coverage for WSLg and ordinary Windows windows if a PowerToys-owned failure is confirmed.
verification: A configured remap behaves consistently in the affected WSLg application and ordinary Windows applications.
Focusing or restarting the WSLg application does not silently disable the remap.
Unrelated WSL and Windows keyboard input remains unchanged.

confidence.rationale: A user reports persistent current-like WSLg behavior, but the PowerToys and WSL versions, exact mapping, and event boundary are unknown.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager mappings reportedly fail in WSLg windows while working in ordinary Windows applications; the thread includes both a one-time failure and a separate persistent report.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.81.1, WSL2 2.1.5.0, WSLg 1.0.60, and Windows build 22631.3737.
The original Caps Lock-to-Ctrl mapping recovered after restarting WSL.
A later commenter reports persistent remapping failures in WSLg windows, including IntelliJ running in WSL, while normal applications work.
The later commenter says restarting WSL, PowerToys, and the computer did not help.
Closed issue #5300 covers WSL1 inside Windows Terminal and was redirected to a Windows Terminal issue.
inferences: The original one-time loss and the later persistent WSLg failure may have different causes.
The WSLg-specific boundary may affect event routing, but no current trace confirms where input stops being remapped.
issue_context.analysis: Do not merge the WSLg symptom with the older WSL1/Windows Terminal case. Ask for the later report's current version and exact mapping, then compare WSLg and Windows windows using that same remap.
initial_investigation: Read the report and all three comments, including the original detailed WSL environment and later persistent WSLg report.
Reviewed closed issue #5300; it uses WSL1 inside Windows Terminal and is not the same WSLg environment.

information_gaps.information: Current PowerToys, Windows, WSL, and WSLg versions for the persistent report, plus the exact source-to-destination mapping and target WSLg application
information_gaps.why_needed: The persistent report is a separate user's symptom and does not provide enough environment or mapping detail to reproduce or identify the input boundary.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the current versions and one exact mapping that fails in a named WSLg application while the same mapping works in a Windows application.

comment.body: The thread contains both the original one-time Caps Lock-to-Ctrl failure and a later report of persistent remap failures in WSLg windows. For the persistent case, could you share the current PowerToys, Windows, WSL, and WSLg versions, one exact source-to-destination mapping, and the WSLg application where it fails?

actions.label: Compare the same remap in WSLg and Windows apps

reproduce.title: Test Keyboard Manager input in a WSLg application
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys with WSL2 and WSLg
prerequisites: A WSL2 distribution with WSLg enabled
A WSLg application and an ordinary Windows application
setup: Configure a simple key-to-key remap and record the PowerToys, Windows, WSL, and WSLg versions.
steps: Invoke the remap in the Windows application and record the result.
Focus the WSLg application and invoke the same remap.
Restart the WSLg application and repeat without changing the Keyboard Manager mapping.
Record whether the failure is limited to one WSLg app or occurs in every WSLg window.
reproduce.expected_result: The same remapping behaves consistently in the Windows and WSLg applications, or the failure is isolated to a specific WSLg input path.
